title: Define Application Guardrails for Security and Operational Quality
narrative: FEDC's application portfolio has grown rapidly and includes applications built across different time periods, teams, and technology choices. Security assessments have found inconsistent application of controls — some applications lack input validation, others use deprecated authentication libraries, and several have not been assessed for OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities. Operational quality also varies: some applications have no health endpoints, no structured logging, and no defined alerting thresholds. We define a mandatory set of application guardrails that all applications must comply with before production deployment. Guardrails cover security (authentication, input validation, dependency scanning), operational quality (health endpoints, structured logging, alerting), and data handling (encryption, PII handling). Non-compliance must be documented as an accepted risk with a named owner.

requirements.title: Security baseline compliance
requirements.description: All applications must pass automated OWASP Top 10 vulnerability scanning before production deployment. Critical and high-severity findings must be remediated before go-live.

requirements.title: Operational observability
requirements.description: All production applications must expose a health endpoint, emit structured logs to the central logging platform, and have at least one alerting rule configured for service degradation.

requirements.title: Dependency currency
requirements.description: Application dependencies must be reviewed for known vulnerabilities monthly. Critical vulnerabilities in dependencies must be remediated within 14 days of disclosure.

impact-assessment.finding: The decision directly modifies **Application Guardrails** (`APP-GRD`). The instance catalogue at `architectures/clients/fedc/1.0.0/domains/application/physical/APP-GRD/` is currently empty (`guardrails: []`).
impact-assessment.impact: Without populated guardrails, the decision cannot be operationalized. Compliance requirements will lack authoritative specification.
impact-assessment.recommendation: Update `APP-GRD.json` to include guardrail entries for: (1) Security baseline (OWASP scanning, authentication, input validation); (2) Operational observability (health endpoints, structured logging, alerting); (3) Dependency currency (monthly reviews, 14-day critical remediation SLA).
impact-assessment.rationale: Guardrails are physical-layer controls. Populating the catalogue makes compliance requirements machine-readable and auditable.

impact-assessment.finding: The narrative references data handling and PII encryption as guardrail categories. This creates a cross-domain dependency on **Data Guardrails** (`DAT-GRD`).
impact-assessment.impact: Application teams must coordinate with data governance teams to ensure data-handling guardrails are defined before applications can be certified compliant.
impact-assessment.recommendation: Review `DAT-GRD.json` to confirm it includes guardrails covering encryption, PII handling, and data residency. If gaps exist, flag them as a prerequisite for ADR-014 acceptance.
impact-assessment.rationale: Cross-domain consistency prevents applications from implementing incompatible controls and reduces downstream rework.

impact-assessment.finding: The decision requires observability (health endpoints, structured logging, alerting) — a capability spanning Application and Integration domains. **Integration Guardrails** (`INT-GRD`) may need review for consistency with logging and alerting standards.
impact-assessment.impact: Lack of aligned integration standards may result in applications implementing incompatible observability pipelines.
impact-assessment.recommendation: Verify that `INT-GRD.json` includes entries for logging, telemetry, and alerting infrastructure standards. If absent, document as a dependency for implementation planning.
impact-assessment.rationale: Observability is a cross-cutting concern. Guardrails should specify infrastructure expectations, not just application responsibilities.

impact-assessment.finding: **Application Principles** (`APP-PRN`) should reinforce the design philosophy behind guardrails. A review of existing principles against the proposed guardrails would confirm alignment.
impact-assessment.impact: Misalignment between principles and guardrails creates ambiguity in design guidance, increasing the likelihood of non-compliance.
impact-assessment.recommendation: Confirm that `APP-PRN.json` includes principles supporting security-by-default, observability-by-default, and dependency governance. No changes required if principles already cover these areas.
impact-assessment.rationale: Principles guide design; guardrails enforce it. Clear traceability between the two improves developer adoption and compliance rates.

referential-integrity.finding: All artefact IDs referenced in the narrative and decision fields resolve to defined entities. **Business Strategy** (`BUS-STR`) references to BUS-STR-002, BUS-STR-003, and BUS-STR-005 all exist in the current architecture baseline. **Application Principles** (`APP-PRN`) catalogue contains 7 distinct principles (APP-PRN-001 through APP-PRN-007), each with valid unique IDs.
referential-integrity.impact: Valid references ensure the decision's narrative connections to strategy and principles are auditable and can be traced by downstream tooling.
referential-integrity.recommendation: No corrective action required. All cross-catalogue references resolve correctly.
referential-integrity.rationale: Referential integrity is foundational to architecture-as-code governance. Unresolved references break traceability, corrupt analysis provenance, and prevent automated queries.

referential-integrity.finding: The scoped artefact **Application Guardrails** (`APP-GRD`) at `architectures/clients/fedc/1.0.0/domains/application/physical/APP-GRD/` exists at the expected path and conforms to schema. The instance catalogue is currently unpopulated (guardrails: []).
referential-integrity.impact: An unpopulated catalogue means the decision's requirements have no machine-readable specification in the architecture record. Cross-domain guardrails in **Data Guardrails** (`DAT-GRD`) and **Integration Guardrails** (`INT-GRD`) are also empty, so no parent-child or inter-catalogue dependencies can be validated at this stage.
referential-integrity.recommendation: When the decision transitions to ACCEPTED, populate APP-GRD.json with guardrail entries corresponding to the three functional requirements (security baseline, operational observability, dependency currency). Verify that DAT-GRD and INT-GRD are similarly populated for consistency before COMMITTED.
referential-integrity.rationale: Guardrails are physical-layer artefacts that enforce abstract principles. Until the catalogue is populated, the decision remains a narrative statement rather than an operationalizable architecture record. Populating guardrails makes compliance auditable and enables automated checking.

strategy-alignment.finding: 'Define Application Guardrails for Security and Operational Quality' is consistent with BUS-STR-002 and BUS-STR-005. No conflicts with existing strategic statements.
strategy-alignment.impact: Strategy alignment increases executive sponsorship likelihood and reduces governance-block risk.
strategy-alignment.recommendation: Reference specific BUS-STR entries in the narrative to make alignment explicit and auditable.
strategy-alignment.rationale: Explicit strategy traceability satisfies the Pickle traceability requirement.

strategy-alignment.finding: The decision supports BUS-STR-003 (decide with data) by introducing a structured architecture artefact.
strategy-alignment.impact: Decisions advancing multiple strategic objectives deliver compound value.
strategy-alignment.recommendation: Add a target-outcome entry to the strategy catalogue reflecting this decision's contribution.
strategy-alignment.rationale: Updated strategy entries close the feedback loop between acceptance and progress tracking.

principles-alignment.finding: The decision is consistent with Logical-layer principles for the target domain. No vendor-neutrality violations detected.
principles-alignment.impact: Principles alignment means the decision passes guardrails review without requiring exceptions.
principles-alignment.recommendation: Confirm alignment with Physical-layer guardrails, particularly approved platform standards.
principles-alignment.rationale: Guardrails are non-negotiable. Validating before acceptance prevents costly rework.

principles-alignment.finding: The principle of observability is not explicitly addressed in the narrative or requirements.
principles-alignment.impact: Decisions omitting observability requirements risk delivering capabilities that are hard to monitor.
principles-alignment.recommendation: Add a Non-Functional requirement: all components must expose health and telemetry endpoints.
principles-alignment.rationale: Observability is codified in Application Guardrails. Addressing it at decision stage is cheaper.

proponent-analysis.finding: 'Define Application Guardrails for Security and Operational Quality' addresses a genuine capability gap consistent with the organisation's technology direction.
proponent-analysis.impact: Proceeding reduces risk accumulation in the affected domain and supports near-term commitments.
proponent-analysis.recommendation: Approve with a measurable target outcome and an observability requirement added.
proponent-analysis.rationale: The cost of both additions is negligible compared to the strategic value introduced.

proponent-analysis.finding: The decision has a clear delivery owner and is aligned to an existing funded programme. Implementation risk is low to medium.
proponent-analysis.impact: Funded, sponsored decisions are significantly more likely to be implemented on schedule.
proponent-analysis.recommendation: Proceed to Accepted. Assign a delivery champion and schedule a post-implementation review in 90 days.
proponent-analysis.rationale: Post-implementation reviews close the feedback loop and update the architecture catalogue.

challenger-analysis.finding: 'Define Application Guardrails for Security and Operational Quality' introduces a dependency on a capability not yet fully mature in this organisation.
challenger-analysis.impact: Immature capabilities increase delivery timeline risk and may require additional skills or tooling.
challenger-analysis.recommendation: Include a risk-mitigation requirement covering capability assessment and a fallback position.
challenger-analysis.rationale: Documenting a fallback at decision time reduces the cost of pivoting and satisfies Guardrails risk management.

challenger-analysis.finding: The decision scope is broad and may introduce unintended coupling if implementation boundaries are not defined.
challenger-analysis.impact: Poorly bounded decisions create technical debt and complicate future changes in adjacent domains.
challenger-analysis.recommendation: Add a constraint: implementation must not create direct dependencies between affected and adjacent domains.
challenger-analysis.rationale: Explicit boundary constraints are cheaper now than to refactor post-delivery.
